lesson: Aggressive DD brake (5/15, min_exp 0.35) on D01+Q07 delivers strong crisis protection (stress 3/3, MDD 26.5%) but destroys return (CAGR 3.5%, IR -0.324). Baltussen et al. 2018 vol-of-vol premium requires sufficient exposure to capture; DD overlay cutting to 35% exposure too aggressively truncates upside. Asness et al. 2019 quality factor (Q07) provides stability but cannot compensate for the return lost to drawdown braking. BM_Corr 0.601 too high for 'diversifier' — reclassify as 'defense'. OOS retention 0.78 confirms no overfitting. Reusable insight: DD 5/15 is too tight for low-vol factor pairs; consider 7/20 or wider to preserve the quality-idiovol return stream while maintaining crisis hedge.
